# Detailed Study Notes — Topic 2: Epithelial Tissue & Cell Junctions ## 1. Structure & Classification of Epithelial Tissues Epithelial tissues cover external body surfaces and line internal organs, ducts, and visceral cavities. ### Classification Scheme: 1. **Simple Epithelium**: Single cell layer resting on basement membrane. 2. **Compound (Stratified) Epithelium**: Multilayered cell sheets designed for protection against mechanical abrasion.

--- ## 2. Simple Epithelial Types ### A. Simple Squamous Epithelium (Pavement Epithelium) - Single layer of flat, tile-like polygonal cells with central oval nuclei. - **Locations**: Endothelium (blood vessels), Mesothelium (pericardial/pleural cavities), Bowman's capsule parietal layer, Pulmonary alveoli.

### B. Simple Cuboidal Epithelium - Cube-shaped cells with central spherical nuclei. - **Locations**: Thyroid follicles, salivary/pancreatic ducts, ovary germinal surface. - **Specialized Brush-Bordered Variant**: Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) of nephron features dense apical microvilli for maximum reabsorption.



### C. Simple Columnar Epithelium - Tall pillar-like cells with basal oval nuclei. - **Locations**: Stomach mucosa, intestinal mucosa (with microvilli and **Goblet Cells** secreting mucin), gall bladder.

### D. Pseudostratified Ciliated Columnar Epithelium - Single cell layer of varying heights giving false appearance of stratification. - **Locations**: Trachea, large bronchi, and nasopharynx.

--- ## 3. Compound (Stratified) Epithelia & Urothelium 1. **Keratinized Stratified Squamous**: Dead keratinized surface scales; forms skin epidermis. 2. **Non-Keratinized Stratified Squamous**: Living moist surface; lines oral cavity, pharynx, oesophagus, vagina, cornea. 3. **Transitional Epithelium (Urothelium)**: Multilayered plastic epithelium with umbrella cells; distensible lining of urinary bladder.



--- ## 4. Epithelial Cell Junctions & Glandular Types | Junction Type | Alternative Name | Key Structural & Functional Role | |---|---|---| | **Tight Junction** | *Zona Occludens* | Fuses plasma membranes; blocks intercellular fluid leakage | | **Adherens Junction** | *Zona Adherens* | Anchors actin filament belts between cells | | **Desmosome** | *Macula Adherens* | Button plaque attached to keratin intermediate filaments; resists shear | | **Gap Junction** | *Nexus* | Connexon channels allowing direct passage of Ca²⁺, Na⁺, and cAMP |
